Geoffrey Wall, of Barrie, Ontario, is alleged to have operated as an airline captain between 2009 and 2025 without a license to fly large commercial passenger planes, according to Peel regional police.

Peruvians go to the polls on Sunday in an election runoff that pits a perennial rightwing candidate, Keiko Fujimori, against a leftist congressman, Roberto Sánchez. Xi Jinping has arrived in North Korea for a two-day trip, his first in nearly seven years, as China’s leader looks to revitalise ties with his junior ally.

Footage published by China’s Xinhua state news agency showed an Air China plane carrying Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, touching down at Pyongyang’s Sunan international airport.

rfi.title: Belfast unrest erupts after stabbing linked to Sudanese refugee
rfi.description: Belfast anti-immigration protesters set vehicles and buildings on fire on Tuesday night, a day after a knife attack allegedly carried out by a Sudanese refugee seriously injured a man and was captured in a graphic video that spread widely online.

rfi.title: Pope Leo to celebrate mass at Barcelona's unfinished Sagrada Familia
rfi.description: Pope Leo XIV will celebrate mass at Barcelona's Sagrada Família on Wednesday and bless its final tower, marking the completion of Antoni Gaudí's masterpiece and making it the tallest church in the world. The pontiff arrived in Spain at the weekend for a week-long visit focused on immigration and politics.

rfi.title: French PM announces measures to combat child abuse amid Lyhanna protests
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu on Tuesday presented initial measures to better protect children, following a meeting with key ministers, in a bid to quell public anger sweeping the country over the death of 11-year-old Lyhanna.

rfi.title: France moves closer to ocean goals with three new marine protection zones
rfi.description: The French government has announced three new marine protected areas, bringing it a step closer to goals established at the 2025 United Nations Ocean Summit. These "strong protection" zones are situated in mainland France, in the French West Indies and the French Southern and Antarctic Lands.

rfi.title: Oxfam warns Europe’s corporate giants are fuelling inequality
rfi.description: Europe’s biggest companies are paying more than two-thirds of their profits to shareholders on average, diverting money that could otherwise support investment, climate action and workers’ wages, according to Oxfam.

rfi.title: Africa's sound, African film at Cannes and the World Cup kick-off
rfi.description: This week, Spotlight on Africa explores cinema and music scoring for African documentary projects with storytellers from Mozambique and Kenya. We will also bring you news from the Cannes Film Festival, along with the African teams selected to take part in the football World Cup.

rfi.title: Platini sues Infantino in French courts as Fifa feud heats up
rfi.description: Former Uefa president Michel Platini said on Monday he is suing Fifa president Gianni Infantino, in the latest chapter of a battle that began when scandal derailed Platini's 2015 bid for the Fifa presidency. After unsuccessful attempts in Switzerland, Platini is now turning to the French justice system to make his case.

rfi.title: Somali football referee denied US entry will miss World Cup debut
rfi.description: The United States has denied entry to football referee Omar Abdulkadir Artan, who had been expected to be the first Somali to officiate a World Cup match.

rfi.title: French star Wembanyama leads Spurs fightback against Knicks
rfi.description: French basketball star Victor Wembanyama scored 32 points as the San Antonio Spurs beat the New York Knicks 115-111 to relaunch their bid for the 2026 NBA crown.

rfi.title: Merz and Macron agree to scrap FCAS joint fighter jet programme
rfi.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and French President Emmanuel Macron have agreed to abandon a joint fighter jet programme due to long-running disagreements between the companies involved, the German government said on Monday.

rfi.title: French NATO jets destroy mystery drone over Latvia as Ukraine war intensifies
rfi.description: French NATO fighter jets stationed in the Baltic region shot down a drone that had entered Latvian airspace on Monday, marking a rare interception under the alliance’s Baltic Air Policing mission. It follows a series of similar incidents linked to the war in Ukraine as Moscow and Kyiv step up drone strikes on each other.

rfi.title: EU says Ebola outbreak makes ceasefire in DRC more necessary than ever
rfi.description: The European Union’s crisis management commissioner has called for a ceasefire between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda, saying the need for peace has become even more urgent with the spread of the Ebola outbreak.

rfi.title: Deschamps tips hat-trick man Olise to make big impact at World Cup
rfi.description: France coach Didier Deschamps challenged forward Michael Olise to make his mark at the World Cup after he hit a hat-trick in a 3-1 World Cup warm-up win over Northern Ireland in Lille on Monday night.

rfi.title: French prosecutors ordered to review all child abuse complaints after girl's murder
rfi.description: French Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin has ordered a review of all complaints involving child victims of sexual violence in France after the death of an 11-year-old girl allegedly killed by a man who had previously been accused of rape and sexual assault of other children but had never been convicted.

euronews.title: This new private island retreat in France is taking wellness to the next level
euronews.description: This sea-facing escape harmonises holistic wellbeing with Mediterranean dining, which includes personalised consultations, tailored treatments across five wellness programmes and three choices of residence – all in one retreat.

euronews.title: Amid outcry against France's courts, who has the most and fewest judges in the EU?
euronews.description: Mounting criticism of France's justice system following the murder of a schoolgirl has revived debate over judicial resources. With judges in short supply, how does Europe compare?

euronews.title: Lombardy's 'Leonardo ferry' has carried commuters for 500 years
euronews.description: The boat designed by Leonardo da Vinci has come back into use after a bridge was closed and traffic increased. The ferry is a model of sustainable transport, powered solely by the river’s current.

euronews.title: EU migration rules kick in, but enforcement is already in doubt
euronews.description: Two years after it was signed, the EU's Pact on Migration and Asylum takes effect this Friday, and the gap between promise and delivery is already wide. Will it hold? Watch the video.

euronews.title: USA: French Air Force display marks 250 years of American independence
euronews.description: France's renowned Patrouille de France performed a symbolic flyover above New York on 9 June. The display launched a series of events marking the upcoming 250th anniversary of the United States Declaration of Independence.

euronews.title: Former Air Canada captain accused of flying for years without the correct license
euronews.description: "Safety was not compromised by this incident because all pilots at Air Canada undergo mandatory recurrent training every six months to validate their flying competency," Air Canada said.

euronews.title: Spain: Human castle welcomes Pope Leo XIV to youth vigil in Barcelona
euronews.description: Welcomed by a towering Catalan human castle, Pope Leo XIV joined 40,000 young people in Barcelona on 9 June, urging greater support for those facing anxiety, loneliness and violence ahead of the blessing of the Sagrada Família's Tower of Jesus Christ.

euronews.title: Newsletter: From K-pop to K2 tanks, South Korea flexes in Europe
euronews.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung visits the Belgian capital on Wednesday for a highly anticipated EU-South Korea Summit. Onlookers expect a buffet of East Asian strength on display, ranging from K-pop toppers to military might, and closer Brussels-Seoul relations.

euronews.title: 'No Lisbon without saints': Popular Saints festivals in the capital
euronews.description: The Popular Saints festivities are back in Lisbon, with Saint Anthony celebrated this Saturday as the city turns into a huge street party with music everywhere.

euronews.title: Heatwaves are killing tens of thousands in India. Officials are barely counting them
euronews.description: Experts warn that official heatwave death figures are grossly underestimated.

euronews.title: Who works the hardest in Europe? The countries with the longest and shortest working weeks
euronews.description: People in some European countries work nearly eight hours more a week than those in others, according to Eurostat. Experts point to collective bargaining, part-time work and economic structure as key drivers of the gap.

euronews.title: Europe Today: US and Iran exchange fresh attacks as EU unveils new Russia sanctions
euronews.description: Iran has launched a missile attack on a US air base in Jordan after President Donald Trump blamed Tehran for the downing of an American Apache helicopter. In Europe, Jorge Liboreiro reports on the EU's new package of sanctions against Russia targeting oil, the Russian "shadow fleet", and banks.

euronews.title: Tech sell-off deepens but oil prices stay flat despite renewed Iran tensions
euronews.description: Global stock markets fell on Wednesday, extending a volatile week driven by concerns about rising inflation, potential interest rate hikes and escalating tensions in the Middle East.

euronews.title: EU monitor warns of 'new normal' following record temperatures in May
euronews.description: Records were broken in Britain, France, Ireland and Portugal last month as a "heat dome" of warm air from northern Africa pushed temperatures well above normal levels across western Europe.

euronews.title: Vehicles set ablaze as anti-immigration protests break out in Belfast following stabbing
euronews.description: Police charged a 30-year-old Sudanese man with attempted murder over the knife attack.

euronews.title: Who gets a seat at the table? UN climate talks slammed over visa delays and shrinking civic space
euronews.description: Climate activists and members of the press are facing unprecedented barriers to one of the most important environmental conferences of the year.

euronews.title: 'Disclosure Day': Will Steven Spielberg deliver an audacious on-screen alien?
euronews.description: Filmmakers have shaped our perception of the unknown, and Steven Spielberg has had aliens on the mind for a while now. He even believes they have been to Earth and may still be amongst us. Will his depiction of alien lifeforms in his anticipated new film 'Disclosure Day' challenge audiences?

euronews.title: Exclusive: ‘If China attacks Taiwan, you will be affected too,’ Taiwan’s deputy FM warns Europe
euronews.description: Euronews Next sat down with Taiwan’s deputy foreign minister Wu Chih-chung in an exclusive interview to talk about the silicon shield and why the world cannot afford to ignore the political tensions.

lemonde.title: Donald Trump se résout à frapper l’Iran pour préserver sa crédibilité
lemonde.description: L’armée américaine a mené une action « proportionnée », le 9 juin au soir, en réponse à l’attaque qui a abattu un hélicoptère Apache près du détroit d’Ormuz. Mais le président des Etats-Unis, qui espère toujours un accord avec Téhéran, semble vouloir éviter l’escalade.

lemonde.title: Mort de Lyhanna : le gouvernement sous le feu des critiques à l’Assemblée nationale
lemonde.description: Entre demande de moyens à gauche et appels à des mesures plus répressives à droite, l’affaire a monopolisé, mardi, les débats parlementaires. De leur côté, les candidats à la présidentielle formulent des propositions pour réformer l’institution judiciaire.

lemonde.title: Patrick Bruel : pourquoi le parquet requiert sa mise en examen et son placement en détention provisoire
lemonde.description: A l’issue de quarante-huit heures de garde à vue, le chanteur devait être présenté à trois juges d’instruction, mercredi, dans la journée.

lemonde.title: Les filières françaises de collecte et de recyclage des déchets en « danger de mort », alertent les acteurs du secteur
lemonde.description: Collectivités, professionnels et ONG mettent en garde le gouvernement contre un risque d’effondrement de l’économie circulaire dans le pays.

lemonde.title: Grève à la SNCF : le trafic régional est fortement perturbé et un TGV sur trois est annulé
lemonde.description: Les cheminots font grève, mercredi, et demandent un moratoire sur l’ouverture à la concurrence ainsi que des hausses de salaire pour faire face à l’inflation.

lemonde.title: En Italie, la fin programmée des albums Panini ajoute au traumatisme de l’absence à la Coupe du monde de football
lemonde.description: Après le Mondial 2030, les célèbres vignettes des joueurs ne seront plus éditées par le groupe d’Emilie-Romagne, mais confiées à l’entreprise américaine Fanatics, a annoncé la FIFA.

lemonde.title: PFAS : l’Agence européenne des produits chimiques entérine la dangerosité du TFA, polluant éternel omniprésent dans l’eau et la chaîne alimentaire
lemonde.description: L’acide trifluoroacétique est désormais officiellement considéré comme « toxique pour la reproduction suspecté ». Une décision qui pourrait avoir des effets en cascade tant cette molécule, la plus petite de la famille des PFAS, est présente dans l’eau potable et les aliments.

lemonde.title: La confiance des Européens dans les Etats-Unis atteint un « niveau historiquement bas », selon un sondage
lemonde.description: A une semaine de la réunion du G7 à Evian, l’enquête paneuropéenne du Centre européen pour les relations étrangères montre que les Européens sont d’accord pour davantage prendre en main leur propre sécurité, sans pour autant souhaiter « divorcer » de l’OTAN.

lemonde.title: SCAF : après l’abandon du projet d’avion de chasse, les perspectives limitées de la coopération de défense franco-allemande
lemonde.description: L’officialisation, lundi, de la fin du projet d’appareil de combat porté par la France et l’Allemagne autour d’Airbus et de Dassault permet aux deux Etats d’aller de l’avant. Mais la plupart des projets envisagés, plus modestes, demeurent flous.

lemonde.title: Visite du pape Léon XIV en Espagne : l’organiste de la Sagrada Familia, maître de musique d’une messe exceptionnelle
lemonde.description: Le souverain pontife est attendu le 10 juin à Barcelone pour l’inauguration de la monumentale tour principale de la basilique imaginée par Antoni Gaudí. Titulaire des grandes orgues, Juan de la Rubia pilote le répertoire musical de la cérémonie.

lemonde.title: « Test cedric » : une notification envoyée par erreur par le Crédit agricole perturbe son application bancaire en ligne
lemonde.description: Dans la foulée de ce message reçu par les utilisateurs mardi en milieu d’après-midi, « l’affluence inhabituellement élevée générée par cet envoi a entraîné des difficultés d’accès à l’application ainsi qu’à certains services », a expliqué la banque. L’application était à nouveau accessible à 19 heures.

lemonde.title: « Les phénomènes climatiques extrêmes sont en train de devenir la norme plutôt que l’exception », alerte l’observatoire européen Copernicus
lemonde.description: De nouveaux records mensuels ont été enregistrés en mai en Europe et ont engendré des situations « particulièrement difficiles » en France, au Royaume-Uni, en Irlande et au Portugal, selon l’observatoire climatique.

lemonde.title: Pourquoi la France a sanctionné le ministre des finances israélien, Bezalel Smotrich
lemonde.description: Faute d’accord au niveau européen, la France et cinq autres pays ont annoncé, mardi 9 juin, le placement sous sanctions du ministre d’extrême droite pour son soutien à l’annexion des territoires palestiniens et les « terribles violences » commises contre les civils palestiniens.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : les dernières informations
lemonde.description: Les dirigeants de huit pays nordiques et baltes, réunis lors d’un sommet en Estonie, ont exprimé leur soutien à l’adhésion de l’Ukraine à l’OTAN et à l’Union européenne dans une déclaration commune.

lemonde.title: A Belfast, violentes manifestations anti-immigration après une attaque au couteau attribuée à un réfugié soudanais
lemonde.description: Des figures d’extrême droite, comme le militant Tommy Robinson, avaient lancé sur les réseaux sociaux des appels à manifester, relayant une vidéo de l’attaque au couteau. « Rien ne peut excuser ni justifier les attaques commises ce soir », a condamné la première ministre nord-irlandaise, Michelle O’Neill.

lemonde.title: En Chine, des chercheurs prestigieux mis en cause par un lanceur d’alerte
lemonde.description: Dans des vidéos sur les réseaux sociaux, l’ancien doctorant et vulgarisateur Geng Hongwei révèle des soupçons de manipulation de données dans les publications de scientifiques chinois de premier plan.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : qui touchera le jackpot financier ?
france24fr.description: La plus grande Coupe du monde de l'histoire du football débute jeudi aux États-Unis, au Canada et au Mexique. La Fifa promet des dizaines de milliards de dollars de retombées économiques, mais les économistes invitent à la prudence.

france24fr.title: Nadège Abomangoli (LFI) : "La justice s'est clochardisée"
france24fr.description: La mort de Lyhanna a fait naitre une grande émotion dans le pays et les politiques s’emparent du sujet des violences faites aux enfants. Pour Nadège Abomangoli, députée LFI de Seine-Saint-Denis et première vice-présidente de l’Assemblée nationale, "les moyens dans la lutte contre les violences faites aux femmes et aux enfants ne sont pas suffisants". Elle estime que "la justice s’est clochardisée". Il sera aussi question du premier meeting de Jean-Luc Mélenchon, candidat à la présidentielle.

france24fr.title: Les collectivités anglaises en banqueroute : les effets du Brexit, dix ans après
france24fr.description: Dix ans sont passés et il fait encore les gros titres au Royaume-Uni. Le Brexit, officialisé lors du référendum du 23 juin 2016, est toujours au cœur des conversations, notamment dans les zones rurales, où le budget des mairies et collectivités a drastiquement baissé. Parfois, les habitants prennent le relais. Nettoyage des rues, entretien des parcs ou travaux de peinture : chacun s'y met pour assurer les services du quotidien. Reportage dans le Yorkshire de nos consœurs de France 2 Maëlys Septe

france24fr.title: le MCC, ce lobby anti-écolo à Bruxelles
france24fr.description: Le MCC Brussels, think tank réactionnaire au cœur de l’Union européenne, lutte contre l’écologie. Les dividendes du pétrole russe financent sa croisade contre le « progressisme ».

france24fr.title: Affaire Patrick Bruel : le parquet requiert la mise en examen et l'incarcération du chanteur
france24fr.description: Le parquet de Nanterre a requis l'ouverture d'une information judiciaire et la mise en examen de Patrick Bruel pour des faits de viols, tentatives de viols, agressions sexuelles et harcèlement sexuel concernant neuf victimes, commis entre 2010 et 2019, selon un communiqué publié ce mercredi matin.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Donnarumma, Foden, Camavinga… un 11 des absents qui ferait trembler les favoris
france24fr.description: Une équipe de joueurs magnifiques mais qui ne prendra pas part à la fête. Entre les joueurs non qualifiés, forfaits et les choix forts des sélectionneurs, France 24 imagine l’équipe type des grands absents de la Coupe du monde 2026 - une équipe alléchante qui aurait pu effectuer un beau parcours au moins jusqu’en demi-finale.

france24fr.title: Le "Match de la mort" : un match de football mythique... au cœur de la propagande soviétique
france24fr.description: Mourir pour avoir osé gagner un match de football ? Ce fut, en Ukraine occupée, le destin de joueurs, qui l'ont emporté contre des nazis, pendant la Seconde Guerre mondiale... Sauf que l'histoire n'est pas aussi simple que ça.

france24fr.title: Football : les Bleues qualifiées pour la Coupe du monde 2027 au Brésil
france24fr.description: L'équipe de France féminine a validé sa qualification pour le Mondial 2027 en battant l'Irlande du Nord. Elle jouera sa cinquième Coupe du monde consécutive.

france24fr.title: Fortune de Jared Kushner, gendre de Trump : "La corruption, on s'en fout"
france24fr.description: À la une de la presse, ce mercredi 10 juin, les affrontements de la nuit à Belfast, où des manifestations ont dégénéré après que des militants d'extrême droite ont appelé à manifester en réaction à une attaque au couteau, notamment sur X, le réseau social d’Elon Musk – qui s’apprête à devenir le premier billionnaire de l’histoire. La fortune, plus modeste, de Jared Kushner. Et la répression au Mozambique contre les opposants et les journalistes.

france24fr.title: Pourquoi le Pentagone a-t-il réduit sa liste de religions pour les soldats américains ?
france24fr.description: Le ministère américain de la Défense a annoncé la semaine dernière la suppression de 180 codes d'affiliation religieuse. Les soldats n'auront désormais le choix qu'entre 31 catégories, dont 22 sont chrétiennes. Si le Pentagone présente cette mesure comme purement administrative, elle s'inscrit dans un agenda idéologique porté par le ministre Pete Hegseth.

france24fr.title: En direct : l'Iran annonce avoir ciblé des bases américaines à Bahreïn et en Jordanie

france24fr.description: Les Gardiens de la révolution iraniens ont annoncé mercredi avoir lancé une attaque de drones contre une base américaine à Bahreïn, après des frappes des États-Unis contre des cibles iraniennes le long du détroit d'Ormuz. Les Gardiens ont ensuite annoncé avoir ciblé une base américaine en Jordanie. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Aux États-Unis, le Congrès octroie 70 milliards de dollars à la lutte contre l'immigration
france24fr.description: Après le Sénat, la Chambre des représentants américaine a approuvé, mardi, un texte budgétaire prévoyant environ 38 milliards de dollars pour la police de l'immigration (ICE), 26 milliards pour la police aux frontières et 5 milliards pour des coûts imprévus. De quoi assurer le financement du programme massif d'expulsions décidé par Donald Trump.

Mondial : à Mexico, des milliers de manifestants ont bloqué l'accès au stade Aztèque
france24fr.description: Le principal accès au stade Aztèque de Mexico, où doivent se tenir jeudi la cérémonie et le match d'ouverture de la Coupe du monde de football 2026, a été bloqué plusieurs heures mardi par des milliers d'enseignants qui manifestent depuis la semaine dernière. La présidente Claudia Sheinbaum a pour l'heure exclu de donner l'ordre à la police de réprimer les manifestations.

france24fr.title: Les Bleues battent l'Irlande et se qualifient pour le Mondial 2027 au Brésil
france24fr.description: L'équipe de France féminine de football ira au Brésil pour la Coupe du monde 2027, après sa qualification mardi soir face à l'Irlande du Nord grâce à un but acrobatique de Melvine Malard.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Adidas va-t-il humilier Nike chez lui ?
france24fr.description: La Coupe du Monde 2026 se joue sur le sol américain, le bastion de Nike, et Adidas a une chance historique de lui prendre son marché, son image et sa domination. Les deux marques ont déjà sorti leurs armes : campagnes marketing aux stratégies opposées, guerre des maillots officiels, éditions limitées et activation digitale à échelle mondiale. Décryptage avec Jonathan Lumbroso, ex-directeur marketing d'Alven, l'un des premiers fonds d'investissement tech en France, et fondateur d'iytro.

france24fr.title: Mondial-2026 : un arbitre somalien refoulé à Los Angeles
france24fr.description: Il s'appelle Omar Artan, il est somalien et avait été désigné meilleur arbitre africain l'an dernier. Pourtant, il a été refoulé samedi à son arrivée aux États-Unis. La Fifa s'est résignée et a annoncé qu'il n'officierait pas durant la Coupe du monde de football. En Somalie, c'est l'indignation.

new-sci.description: Mice seemed to reap some of the benefits of sleep by having their brain activity stimulated while they were awake, and the researchers plan to test the approach on people

new-sci.title: Are we getting to the point where it's safe to gene-edit babies?
new-sci.description: A team in the US has reported promising results after using an improved form of CRISPR to gene-edit human embryos, but a major issue remains unsolved

new-sci.title: The maths meme that has been distracting mathematicians for a century
new-sci.description: A seemingly simple set of rules kicks off a kind of mathematical magic trick, which has kept great minds busy since the 1930s. Columnist Jacob Aron explores the origins of the Collatz conjecture, why it is so addictive to mathematicians and whether AI could help us solve it once and for all

phys-org.title: Italian astronaut to pilot Artemis III mission
phys-org.description: Italian astronaut Luca Parmitano is hoping to bring a taste of his homeland to the Artemis III mission, which he will pilot near Earth in 2027 to test two lunar modules.

phys-org.title: To discover new physics, AI may need to 'unlearn' the old one
phys-org.description: A study in the Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics explores how a machine-learning strategy known as transfer learning could dramatically reduce the computational cost of searching for new physics beyond the standard cosmological model—while also revealing an unexpected risk: Sometimes AI systems can become too reliant on what they already know.

phys-org.title: Study finds fishing bycatch does not attract lesser black-backed gulls out of wind farms
phys-org.description: Lesser black-backed gulls from the colony on the Dutch island of Neeltje Jans appear to avoid the wind farm off the Zeeland coast, with the exception of some males. NIOZ ecologist Rosemarie Kentie and her colleagues suspected the gulls were attracted by fishing boats outside the wind farm and the bycatch thrown overboard. This turned out not to be the case: Even during weekends, when there is little fishing, the birds rarely visit the wind farm.

phys-org.title: Theoretical model developed to understand how isotopes change spectroscopy results
phys-org.description: When researchers want to uncover what atoms make up a material, they turn to a number of tried-and-true spectroscopy methods. Spectroscopy works by shining a specific type of light onto a substance and then analyzing how that light is either absorbed, emitted, or scattered. Every atom has a different way of interacting with light, and scientists study this light-matter interaction to identify the atoms in the material.

phys-org.title: Survival of five million amphibians and reptiles displaced by construction in British Columbia may not be tracked
phys-org.description: UBC researchers have found that more than five million amphibians and reptiles were displaced by development in British Columbia in just four years—and that there is no requirement to monitor survival rates. The paper published in the Journal of Wildlife Management is the first of its kind to document the large-scale herpetofauna relocation taking place in the province.

phys-org.title: How health care systems shape native preferences for immigrants
phys-org.description: In recent years, anti-immigration sentiment has become increasingly common around the world. A common concern surrounding immigration is its potential impact on the host country's welfare system, including health care. Such concerns can reduce public support for accepting immigrants and for redistributive welfare policies.

phys-org.title: Strong leadership will be key as AI reshapes the workforce, argues research
phys-org.description: As artificial intelligence changes how work gets done, experts say strong leadership will play a critical role in helping employees adapt to shifting responsibilities, evolving technologies and changing workplace demands. The findings are published in the journal Human Resource Development Review.

phys-org.title: Physicists harness potential of quantum phase transitions
phys-org.description: Researchers at University College Dublin and international collaborators have just published a detailed and accessible guide that aims to translate theoretical ideas into practical devices for quantum enhanced sensing technologies.

phys-org.title: Satellite data reveal hidden labor trafficking in Brazil
phys-org.description: A Stanford team used geospatial data and detection algorithms to achieve a tenfold increase in rescues from modern slavery in the Brazilian Amazon. Now, they are planning to expand their approach.

phys-org.title: Examining doctoral students' attitudes toward AI chatbots and ChatGPT use in higher education
phys-org.description: Researchers from the University of Phoenix College of Doctoral Studies have published research examining graduate students' attitudes toward artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots and their reported use of ChatGPT in higher education environments. The article, "Relationship between Students' Attitudes toward Artificial Intelligence (AI) and their usage of AI Chatbots," appears in the International Journal of AI in Pedagogy, Innovation, and Learning Futures.

phys-org.title: How 'undone science' shaped Chile's glacier protection battle
phys-org.description: What is "undone science," and how does it affect environmental policy and regulation around the world? In a recent study published in Tapuya: Latin American Science, Technology and Society, Javiera Barandiarán, an associate professor in global studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and colleagues trace how undone science has shaped conflicts between mining and glacier conservation over the past two decades in Chile. The authors show how missing areas of scientific knowledge, whe

phys-org.title: Neutron-rich nuclei yield beta-decay clues that could refine heavy-element origin models
phys-org.description: How are heavy elements formed in the universe? Extremely neutron-rich atomic nuclei and their beta-decay rates play an important role in this process. Until now, it has been very difficult to determine these rates experimentally. Researchers at TU Darmstadt have developed theoretical predictions for such processes and successfully compared them with experimental data, where they exist. The results were published in Physical Review Letters.

phys-org.title: NASA unveils Artemis III astronauts to test technology for a future moon landing
phys-org.description: NASA on Tuesday revealed the crew for its Artemis III mission, the next step in the space agency's plan to eventually land astronauts on the moon.

phys-org.title: Physicists observe synchronized quantum dance of excitons and phonons
phys-org.description: An international team of researchers has reported a major advance in understanding quantum dynamics in semiconductor materials. They directly observed how excitons and phonons evolve together in perovskite nanocrystals, revealing a fully coherent quantum dance between light-induced electronic excitations and crystal lattice vibrations. They published their findings in Nature Communications.

phys-org.title: Quality of relationship between patient and therapist is key to preventing child sex offenders from doing it again
phys-org.description: Since the 1980s, there has been extensive research on the effectiveness of treatment for perpetrators of sexual crimes against children. Studies have examined rehabilitation programs, the role of clinicians and the factors associated with recidivism. However, what remains unclear is how these factors interact to influence recidivism once treatment is over.

phys-org.title: Freshwater boundary breach deepens as climate and land use amplify extremes
phys-org.description: Human activities have significantly altered the freshwater cycle, threatening its ability to support vital climatic and ecological Earth system processes. A new study led by researchers at the University of Eastern Finland shows that the freshwater cycle has increasingly moved away from a stable state due to climate change and large-scale water and land use. The newly published study updates the status of the freshwater change planetary boundary, which is one of the core components in the annual

phys-org.title: Brain removal in Iron Age Scotland burial reveals far-reaching family ties
phys-org.description: It is difficult to identify funerary practices in Iron Age (c. 800 BC–AD 43) Britain, as human remains rarely survive. However, evidence is particularly prominent in north-west Scotland, because environmental conditions support the preservation of bone. To take advantage of this, a team of researchers from the U.K. and U.S. examined two individuals (one adult female and one juvenile male) buried in a low stone cairn at Loch Borralie in Sutherland, close to the north-west extremity of the Scottis

phys-org.title: Why vague conservation targets are failing some vulnerable species
phys-org.description: A shift toward more precise, measurable conservation goals could hold the key to protecting vulnerable species, according to the findings of a new study looking at African elephants. Conservationists are often faced with difficult decisions about where to put their financial resources; invest where populations are largest or where declines are fastest? Or invest in multiple smaller sites to maintain a species' range?

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

proj-syn.title: Big Tech’s Shadow Market Power
proj-syn.description: Big Tech firms are amassing market power through strategies that bypass current rules for oversight, investigation, and intervention. Unless and until regulators account for the full scope and scale of these strategies, Silicon Valley’s dominance will remain unchallenged.

proj-syn.title: The AI Revolution Mirrors the Green Transition
proj-syn.description: The need for massive upfront investments and the likelihood of significant job displacement imply remarkable parallels between the AI buildout and the green transition. In both cases, the state has an important role to play in guiding market forces on behalf of the public good.

proj-syn.title: Where Is China’s Trillion-Dollar Trade Surplus Going?
proj-syn.description: Whereas China’s trade surplus used to be absorbed largely by the central bank and channeled into official reserves, it is now being redeployed by private actors in search of yield. This indicates China’s progress on financial deepening and underscores markets' increasingly central role in shaping the economy.

proj-syn.title: The Future of Development Finance Is Not Primarily About Money
proj-syn.description: Multilateral development banks have not kept pace with changes to the global financial environment. For middle-income countries like India, accessing knowledge and technology is now a bigger challenge than raising capital, which suggests that these institutions must rethink their operating model.

proj-syn.title: Nigeria’s Perilous French Gambit
proj-syn.description: Nigeria’s increasingly close relationship with France marks a departure from six decades of foreign policy aimed at reducing French influence in West Africa. An increasingly close relationship with a power that has long sought to undermine Nigerian influence in West Africa will benefit only politically connected business elites.

proj-syn.title: Autocracy Is Fueling Mexico’s Fiscal Deterioration
proj-syn.description: Mexico’s recent ratings downgrades are merely a symptom of a more serious malady: the ruling Morena party’s efforts to consolidate power permanently. To ensure the legal predictability foreign investors require, President Claudia Sheinbaum would need to confront Morena’s ideological legacy and, more importantly, its cartel ties.

proj-syn.title: The Trump Economy Is Bad News for Republicans
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump triumphed in the 2024 election by continually hammering on the Biden administration’s dismal inflation record. If his party gets shellacked in this year’s midterm elections, it will be because he has made Americans even worse off.

proj-syn.title: SpaceX Is the New East India Company
proj-syn.description: Although SpaceX is not about to rule over foreign subjects, as the chartered companies founded in the early modern era did, it, too, is operating beyond the reach of any sovereign. And like its predecessors, it has already accumulated immense powers that governments will struggle to reclaim.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Should Not Raise Interest Rates Yet
proj-syn.description: Against a backdrop of acute uncertainty, weak growth, subdued wages, and elevated market interest rates, monetary tightening is warranted only when there is convincing evidence that higher inflation is becoming entrenched. No such evidence has yet materialized in Europe.

proj-syn.title: When Markets Run on Empty
proj-syn.description: Markets are flying high despite geopolitical turmoil because a broad-based willingness to keep spending has been matched by an ability to keep doing so. But as more economic participants exhaust their means and rely on debt, a painful moment of truth will arrive—sooner rather than later if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

proj-syn.title: The Pope and the AI Profiteers
proj-syn.description: In his first encyclical, Pope Leo XIV rightly rejects the idea that markets alone can be trusted to shape society’s technological future. Recognizing that AI raises questions that prices and profits cannot answer, the Chicago-born pope has posed a direct challenge to Chicago School economics.

proj-syn.title: AI Must Not Encroach on Human Dignity
proj-syn.description: In a world captivated by technological advances, Pope Leo XIV’s first encyclical seeks to shift attention away from the marvels and terrors of AI and toward the magnificence of humanity. The message that the technology lacks a “moral conscience” and is distinct from human cognition is necessary and welcome.

proj-syn.title: The Key Forces Now Shaping Markets and Geopolitics
proj-syn.description: Three major factors are likely to shape economic and geopolitical outcomes over the next several years: politically unconstrained AI development, a shift from the logic of globalization to zero-sum thinking, and heightened international tail risks. Much could go right, or at least as expected—until it doesn’t.

proj-syn.title: The Living Ghosts of Violent Radicalism
proj-syn.description: Following World War II, the most militant student movements emerged in the former Axis powers as a way to cope with previous generations' complicity. But while the Red Army Faction and others were haunted by memories of past crimes, today's young people have mostly forgotten, and a growing number think far-right politics are cool.

proj-syn.title: Using AI to Test Policy Language
proj-syn.description: Policymakers have long understood that language affects economic behavior, but until recently, there were few tools capable of systematically analyzing its effects. AI may now help close that gap, enabling officials to anticipate how framing and timing can move markets and shift public opinion.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Competitiveness Bogeyman
proj-syn.description: Calls for European leaders to protect domestic industry from "unfairly" subsidized Chinese competition have lately grown louder. But while tariffs might offer temporary relief to a few sectors, they cannot restore Europe's technological leadership, industrial dynamism, or export competitiveness.

proj-syn.title: Putting American Science on a MAGA Leash
proj-syn.description: A draft rule from US President Donald Trump’s White House Office of Management and Budget would subject all scientific research funding to the whims of political appointees, further undercutting a pillar of American power. The goal is to foreclose any future that is plural, contestable, and beyond the president’s control.

proj-syn.title: How Measles Came Roaring Back
proj-syn.description: Bangladesh is facing soaring measles cases not because of a single localized failure, but because of years of systemic erosion. Ultimately, maintaining herd immunity against highly contagious viruses requires relentless attention to supply and demand, as well as to the broader social and institutional foundations of public health.
